dialog.body: Public Works storm line, this is Kevin, what's going on?

Oh good, somebody picked up. I wasn't sure, it's Sunday, City Hall's shut, I figured I'd get a machine. Anyway. This is Siobhan McCarthy, I'm at 12 Brewer Street, down the Fifth Ward, and the drain out front of my house is acting up again.
Okay, Siobhan McCarthy, 12 Brewer... Street. Fifth Ward. Got it. Acting up how?

Gurgling. Like a drain in a tub, you know that noise? Glug glug. And it's spitting water back up over the top and right onto the sidewalk. I went out to get the paper this morning, well, what was left of the paper, it was soaked through, the kid throws it in the bushes no matter what, I've told him, anyway, I step off the stoop and the water's up to my ankles in the street. Ankles. Cars going by throwing wakes like it's the harbor.
Wakes, yeah, I've been hearing that a lot today. This storm dumped a ton since yesterday. Is any of it getting into the house?

No, no, the house is fine, bone dry, I checked. It's the street. It's the curb. It's up to the top of the curb out there. Which, you know, I've been in this house eleven years and it never used to do this. Now it's every storm.
Okay. House dry, street backed up to curb height, catch basin gurgling and overflowing onto the sidewalk. Writing all that down.
And here's my question. Has anybody else called about Brewer Street? Because I can't be the only one standing out there in my boots.
Let me look. [pause] So I've got a call from January twenty-ninth, a Judith Gardiner, same address actually.
That's my tenant, she's up in the in-law unit over the garage. She called? Good for her. And?
And a crew went out February second and cleared the grate at the corner. Leaves and debris.

Cleared the grate. Wonderful. So they swept off the top and here we are again. Lot of good that did. Speaking of Judith, she drives a school bus, she knocked on my door an hour ago to tell me there's an early dismissal tomorrow, which, nobody told me, not that I've got anybody in school, but I'm supposed to move my car so she can get hers out early, so now I've got that to deal with too. Where was I. The grate. Somebody should look under the grate, not just on it.

Yeah, I hear you. I'm putting a note that this is the second time from this address and the last visit was just the grate. Okay, so I'm logging a catch basin backup at 12 Brewer and I've got a crew down to clear the drain tomorrow, Monday the twenty-third.
Tomorrow. And they'll do more than brush the leaves off this time?
I'm writing it in the notes so they see it. Prior visit grate only, still backing up. That's what they'll be reading when they pull up.
Fine. Tell them to park on the other side, my car's getting moved for the bus situation. Honestly. Alright, Kevin, thank you, enjoy your Sunday in there.
Ha, doing my best. Stay out of the puddles, Siobhan.
